en.html:
The coast was cool today.
Compared with yesterday, it might have been another world. Still too warm for the season on the calendar, but chilly enough to make short sleeves uncomfortable.

The locals merely sighed at this extraordinary change in temperature. Gloomily. This too happened often, they told me.
...Since Enoshima had gone <ruby>wrong<rt>・・・・</rt></ruby>.

Ichijou and I stood side by side, looking across at the island.
We would infiltrate it at night. Until then, I would have liked to gather what information I could. But there were no bathers today, and the businesses serving them were shut. Poor conditions for inquiries.

Wasted time was regrettable. Nothing could be done about it, however.
We could only wait, without impatience.

en.html:
She was not describing her own feelings. I understood that at once.
She meant the scene around us.

Before noon, this shore ought to have been busy with people fishing. Instead: boats that never put to sea, a few fishermen merely looking out over the water—and desolation.

Perhaps this was Katase Beach's true face now. Yesterday's bustle had been staged by people with no connection to the place.

Lovely Enoshima had been taken from them. Its gateway, too, was withering.
<ruby>Why<rt>why</rt></ruby>?

en.html: An indictment impossible to deny. —Yes. Rokuhara's tyranny was wrong. Search any government for faults, and there would be no end to them. Even rulers like Rokuhara were better than none. Given the state of the world, military rule could hardly be avoided.◆ ...Arguments in Rokuhara's defense were plentiful. But what barrier could such clever reasoning put in the path of this needle-straight, unhesitating accusation? However one dressed it up, they were wrong. They were committing wrongs. The wrong of inhumanity. Those clever defenses did not truly protect the shogunate. They protected the speaker—from the helplessness and humiliation of being unable to condemn its wrongs to its face. This girl would not spare them a glance. She turned away neither from the enemy's evil nor from her own powerlessness. She sought to carry the truth through. A strengthstrength almost uncanny.
en.text:
An indictment impossible to deny.

—Yes. Rokuhara's tyranny was wrong.

Search any government for faults, and there would be no end to them.
Even rulers like Rokuhara were better than none.
Given the state of the world, military rule could hardly be avoided.◆
...Arguments in Rokuhara's defense were plentiful.

But what barrier could such clever reasoning put in the path of this needle-straight, unhesitating accusation?
However one dressed it up, they were wrong. They were committing wrongs.
The wrong of inhumanity.

Those clever defenses did not truly protect the shogunate. They protected the speaker—from the helplessness and humiliation of being unable to condemn its wrongs to its face.
This girl would not spare them a glance.

She turned away neither from the enemy's evil nor from her own powerlessness. She sought to carry the truth through.
A strengthstrength almost uncanny.

否定の仕様もない弾劾。
　
　――そう。六波羅の圧政は、間違っている。

　どのような政府でも瑕瑾を探せばきりがない、
　六波羅のような統治者でもいないよりはまし、
　現今の世界情勢を思えば軍事政権もやむなし、◆
　……六波羅とて、弁護の余地はいくらでもある。

　が、そんな賢しらな理屈が、この針の如く迷いない
弾劾に対して、何の壁になるだろう。
　どう言い繕おうが、彼らが間違っているのは事実な
のだ――誤りを犯しているのは事実なのだ。

　非道という誤りを。

　小賢しい弁護はその実、幕府を守るためのものでは
なく、面と向かって幕府の誤りを非難できない無力感、
屈辱感から己を守るためのものである。
　そんなものに、この少女は一顧だにくれない。

　敵の邪悪からも己の無力からも目を逸らさず、真実
を貫徹せんとする。
　それは異奇なまでの、勁つよさといえた。

Kageaki"Shall we turn back?"

Kageaki"We can look at it on the way back."
Kanae"Haaye, what a natural talent. A lady's heart beneath your feet, and you don't even notice the bump... So wonderfully obtuse. I am quite, quite dizzy."
Kageaki"Are you unwell, Captain?"
Kanae"Your charm is confusing me, Mr. Kageaki. Is this... love?"
Kageaki"A misapprehension. Please retain your composure."
Kanae"Just standing here beside you, such palpitations! My heart is not listening to me only... Ah, whatever can be the matter?"
Kageaki"Possibly a cardiac disorder. Please consult a physician."
Kanae"Not THAT...! This garden of thorns in my breast—surely one sincere word from Mr. Kageaki would...!"
Kageaki(A sincere word...)
Kanae"..."
Kageaki"You are not in your right mind."
Kanae"Achha. Sincerity received. That will do. Let us rest a little."
Kageaki"Certainly."

Kageaki"I am glad you found it amusing. No humor was intended."
Kanae"Yes... most entertaining. Truly."
Kanae"In return, let me tell you an entertaining story."
Kageaki"..."
Kanae"Once upon a time, deep in the mountains, there lived a demon."
Kanae"An enormously strong demon. Boar and bear were no match for it. In time, people feared it as lord of the mountain."
Kanae"Then it turned its eyes toward the villages. Humans, too, must be shown how strong it was."
Kanae"Down it came, and laid waste to a village at the mountain's foot. People were killed. Homes destroyed. The survivors were left to bear what it had done."
Kanae"All this, the demon did with the greatest delight・・・."
Kageaki"..."
Kanae"But the lord governing that village was a brave samurai. Boldly he stood against the demon, to protect his people."
Kanae"The demon was strong. Again and again the lord was defeated and wounded. Still he would not give up. At last, with a mountain hermit's help, he killed it."
Kanae"Everyone rejoiced. Then, before long, a troublesome matter came to their attention."
Kanae"Some survivors, they decided, had been tainted by the demon. The danger was not over, they said. Those people carried it with them. Such was the verdict."
Kanae"So the lord gathered those survivors and burned them to death. Most reluctantly・・・・, of course. The hermit had advised it: their souls must be purified of the demon's defilement."
Kageaki"..."
Kanae"And peace returned to the village. The lord was worshipped as a living god. After his death they enshrined him, and he became a god in truth."
Kanae"And they all lived happily ever after."
